stories.title: Trump Appoints Stephen Miller as New Chief of Staff Following Midterm Losses
stories.summary: Donald Trump has announced that Stephen Miller will replace Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff. Wiles, who served for 21 months and was the first woman to hold the position, is stepping down after significant Republican losses in the recent midterm elections. Miller, known for his controversial role in shaping the administration's immigration policies, will take on the top advisory role.

stories.title: Thomas Markle Sr. Arrested in Florida on Child Abuse Material Charges
stories.summary: Thomas Markle Sr., the estranged father of Meghan Markle, was arrested by federal agents in Florida on charges related to the possession of child sexual abuse material. The arrest follows an investigation that began after his son reportedly discovered boxes containing numerous images at his father's former home in the Philippines. Meghan Markle expressed that she is 'deeply distressed' by the charges against her father.

stories.title: Kenyan Cult Leader Paul Mackenzie Sentenced to 200 Years for Mass Murders
stories.summary: Paul Mackenzie, the leader of a Kenyan doomsday cult, has been sentenced to 200 years in prison for the murders of 190 children and one adult. He was convicted for inciting his followers to starve themselves to death as part of a belief that they would meet Jesus. The court's decision follows a trial that included 28 co-defendants, and Mackenzie plans to appeal.

stories.title: California Governor Commutes All Death Sentences to Life Without Parole
stories.summary: California Governor Gavin Newsom announced that he will commute the sentences of all 548 death row inmates in the state to life in prison without the possibility of parole. He stated that capital punishment is morally wrong, and the state Supreme Court will have the final authority on these cases.

stories.title: Mass Protests Erupt in Paraguay Over Banking Scandal and Impeachment of President Peña
stories.summary: Thousands of Paraguayans are protesting against a banking scandal that has left nearly half the population unable to access their savings. Demonstrators are calling for the impeachment of President Santiago Peña, who has offered to resign amid the crisis. However, Congress has put his resignation on hold as impeachment proceedings continue.

Iran has claimed responsibility for the attack, which is part of a broader escalation of assaults on shipping in the region, including two other vessels that were reported to be on fire.
